messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for routing-service in eu-west-1. 15% error rate over 5m. Trigger: policy-evaluator.err-rate > 10%

pagerduty-bot: Paged: jamie (oncall) - ack required

jamie (oncall): acked, looking. pulling logs now. @sofia can you join?

sofia (sre): on it. seeing a bunch of model selection errors: 'variant-mismatch' and 'fallback-loop' in the policy-evaluator logs.

dani (eng-runtime): quick note — we rolled the config/schema migration at 03:10 which removed the deprecated field `preferred_variant` and introduced `variant_selector` with default `allow_fallback: true`. could that be it?

matt (infra): spike correlates with the migration time. graphs show repeated cross-region failovers from eu-west-1 -> us-east-1, causing overloaded hosts in us-east.

jamie (oncall): customer impact? any external-facing errors or timeouts?

kevin (support): CS reported 3 customers with degraded chat responses in EU and increased latency, one request timed out. No billing impact reported yet.

sofia (sre): root cause hypothesis: many configs relied on `preferred_variant: v1` to force the primary model. the new schema left that unset for older configs, runtime defaulted to permissive fallback. when v1 capacity dipped, the selector kept failing over between variants and regions -> oscillation (fallback loop).

dani (eng-runtime): pulling the effective config from the store for an affected customer. current live blob looks like this:

```json
{
  "variant_selector": {
    "allow_fallback": true,
    "regions": ["eu-west-1","us-east-1"],
    "default_policy": "auto"
  },
  "deprecated": { "preferred_variant": null }
}
```

jamie (oncall): can we hotfix? set allow_fallback=false or pin default_policy=strict for eu-west?

matt (infra): yes, we can push a runtime override for eu-west-1 to disable cross-region fallback. prepping change now.

sofia (sre): also recommend we revert the schema mapping for configs that had `preferred_variant` set so the runtime respects it; otherwise silent defaults are dangerous.

dani (eng-runtime): applied temporary override: set `variant_selector.allow_fallback=false` for the eu-west-1 scope. command I ran:

```bash
rctl config set --scope region:eu-west-1 variant_selector.allow_fallback=false --reason 'mitigate fallback loop'
```

incident-bot: action recorded. Change ID: cfg-8921. Notifying autoscaler and routing monitors.

matt (infra): rolling out override to edge nodes now (zone-by-zone).

jamie (oncall): monitoring... error rate dropping 10% -> 2% in 6m.

sofia (sre): latency trending back to baseline. still seeing a handful of stale retry attempts from clients that hit the loop earlier.

kevin (support): CS has been updated. ticket created: CS-1129. informing affected customers with temporary mitigation note.

dani (eng-runtime): root cause confirmed: the migration script didn't map null `preferred_variant` to an explicit `preferred_variant: none` or `pin_primary: false`. runtime treated missing field as 'allow_any', which combined with `allow_fallback=true` caused oscillation when capacity pressure existed. patching migration to emit explicit fields.

sofia (sre): next steps: revert the schema's silent-default behavior, add a validation warning for deprecated fields, and add an automated test to catch default-policy regressions during migrations.

jamie (oncall): handing off to night oncall @sofia for verification and watch. i'll be available until 01:00 UTC for questions.

sofia (sre): taking handoff. will monitor for 2 hours. if error rate > 5% re-escalate to P0.

incident-bot: status -> Monitoring. Incident ref: INC-2026-315. Duration so far: 28m.

matt (infra): postmortem actions: add canary for config migrations (deploy to 1% of tenants), and make migrations no-op if they change default policy semantics.

dani (eng-runtime): will open MR with migration patch + runtime guard rails and a test that detects when a migration changes runtime-defaults. draft PR: https://git.redwood/infr/runtime/merge-requests/345

kevin (support): customer impact summary for the report: 3 customers affected in EU, degraded latency and some 5xxs, no data loss. CS recommends goodwill credits if SLA breached.

jamie (oncall): good work. thank you all for the quick mitigation. closing thread in 1h if stable. :thumbsup:
